uncited: **Inputs:** A set of extracted surface meshes from independent sub-blocks of a volume dataset; the hierarchical tree structure of the spatial decomposition (octree or similar).
**Outputs:** A unified, manifold isosurface mesh dumped to disk.
*   **Node Type:** An enumeration representing the position of a node relative to its father's split plane.
*   Z-split: `front`, `bottom` (or `back`)
*   **Ancestry Set:** For a node $n$ in a tree rooted at $p$, the set of nodes containing $n$ and its recursive fathers up to $p$.
Determine the type of each node based on the split direction of its father.
If a node $p$ is split along the x-axis, its children are typed `left` and `right`.
Identify vertices shared between adjacent blocks.
Due to numerical inaccuracies in vertex extraction, coordinate comparison is unreliable.
Instead, use the property of the Marching Cubes algorithm: a cell edge can generate at most one point.
Determine if a completed block $p_1$ can merge with another block $p_2$ (brother) or $n$ (nephew, i.e., a child of $p_1$'s brother).
This criterion ensures that the blocks share a true geometric boundary and do not overlap or touch only at corners/edges in a way that violates manifold constraints.
After merging the meshes, simplify the "pasted area" (the interface) using the same error criteria $E_0$ used during extraction.
Prevent edge contractions if the "time lag sphere" (centered on the edge midpoint with radius $rad(c)$) is not fully included in the merged blocks.
When two brothers are merged, their father node is considered completely processed.
*   **Ancestry Check:** When merging a nephew, it is critical to check *all* ancestors of the nephew up to the brother node.
*   **Processing Order:** When two brothers are merged, their father is marked completely processed.
*   **Time Complexity:** The merge eligibility check requires traversing the ancestry of nodes, which is $O(h)$ where $h$ is the height of the tree.
The actual mesh merging and simplification depend on the number of triangles at the boundary.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the tree structure and the meshes of completed blocks until they are merged or dumped.
Restricted Adjacency Merging was introduced in the context of parallel isosurface extraction for very large geophysical datasets.
